To login with a current World of Warships / Wargaming account:

1. dl the STEAM World of warships client. http://store.steampowered.com/app/552990/

2. run the application once, when you get to the login screen...DO NOTHING! exit the application completely by hitting the little "X" in the top right hand corner of the window.

3. go to your WoWs folder in STEAM. Example: local disk (C:)>Program Files (x86)>STEAM>steamapps>common>World of Warships

4. In that folder, there will be an application extension file that should be called "steam_api.dll". Right click on that file, click "rename", and put a "2" in front of the name (2steam_api.dll) press "enter.

5. Close folder. Restart your game from STEAM. And now you should have the option to log in with your existing account.

I don't have much time on Steam, because I'm playing it using the publisher's own launcher a long time before it come on Steam. But I have multiple top tier ships and a lot of other "high end" stuff (T9 premium ship, legendary captains, permanent camouflage...). The way Wargaming managing the game was fine during my first year, but since my 2nd year (2018) until this moment, they are going further and further down the scummy path.

What scummy path, you ask? False advertising "this ship can be earn for free" then slapped the player across the face with an inhumanly grind that normal people would take a few months to one year to finish, but they condensed the grind into 28 days. Releasing OP ship for cash money, sell it, then remove that ship because it's too OP and bad for game balance, then put that ship in a loot box and use that ship OP-ness (as well as many other OP ship that were removed earlier) to advertising that loot box. Trying to release an outrageously bad fuction (search "naval training center" if you want to know more) and only backed down when an outrage happened, but that could be just an anchor to release another bad fuction because it's "not as bad as previous one". And more, I just don't bother remembering them all.

The gameplay is still fine, though. So there is that.
